summary: Fremont Peak lookout planned in 1930-31 and under work in 1934; FFLA lists it gone, and the peak is now a state park open to the public with no source describing remains.

facts.status_note: FFLA lists the tower as gone; no source describes what, if anything, remains on the summit

access.note: Fremont Peak State Park offers day-use and overnight camping; the observatory holds public programs on select evenings

events.note: Rock lookout house announced for the peak with a telephone line from San Juan; completion not confirmed in the sources read
Work under way on the peak; planned fire trails, roads and a fire outlook building; land passed from San Benito County to the State Park Commission
Fremont Peak State Park established on 162 acres

notes_for_editor: Whether the 1930s lookout was built is not confirmed in the sources read; the record kind 'tower' conflicts with the 1931 plan for a rock lookout house and the 1934 fire outlook building. The '(Military)' label in the record and FFLA is not explained by any source read. The ranger is Hiram Wyman in the Nov 1930 article and H.E. ("Hi") Wyman in the Apr 1931 article; the story says we could not settle which is right. Elevation differs: 3,169 ft (BenitoLink, State Parks) vs 3,173 ft (Wikipedia), so no height is recorded. The State Parks page reports a proposal to rename the park tooyohtak, with public comment through 2026-10-23; not in the story. A 1931 brush-fire report from the King City Rustler could not be read (cdnc.ucr.edu returned 403).
